tables.description: This table records the usage count of different AI models in the AI Playground. Usage is tracked per user and per model; that is, each user has a separate count for each model. The usage count is used to enforce quotas and is reset daily by a scheduled job.

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: Surrogate primary key. Uniqueness of records is enforced by users_pk1 and model_name.

columns.name: users_pk1
columns.description: Foreign key to users.pk1.

columns.name: model_name
columns.description: AI model for which usage count and quota are tracked, e.g. AMAZON_NOVA_MICRO, AMAZON_NOVA_LITE. This is represented as an int for easier querying and indexing, and the mapping of int to model name is maintained in the application code. The default 0 denotes None for backward compatibility.

columns.name: usage_count
columns.description: The number of times the user has used the model in the AI Playground. This count is used to enforce usage quotas.

tables.description: This is the table that tracks user activity. Almost every page a user visits in your system gets recorded here. It is like your apache access logs but with better user tracking.

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: This is the type of activity. Groups the event based on what occurred. For example, TAB_ACCESS (page view), PAGE_ACCESS (page view, Triggered when a page, other than a course, organization, content, module, or tab is accessed on the system. The name of the navigation item will be returned.), LOGIN_ATTEMPT, LOGOUT, SESSION_TIMEOUT, COURSE_ACCESS (Page view, Triggered when a course frameset is loaded, or when a page is accessed in a course. The name of the navigation item will be returned.), SESSION_INT (Triggered when a session is initialized), etc. The full list of values is in the TrackingEvent.Type enumueration.

columns.name: user_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].users table to indicate the owner of the activity. This can be NULL if the user cannot be determined. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1.

columns.name: course_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign ley referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].course_main table to indicate the Course the activity is occuring in. This will be NULL if the activity occurs outside a Course. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1.

columns.name: group_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the group table to indicate the Course Group this activity belongs to. This will be NULL if the activity is not Course Group related.

columns.name: forum_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the forum table to indicate the Forum this activity is taking place in. Forum activity can take place within a Course or Institution Discussion Board. This will be NULL if the activity takes place outside a Forum.

columns.name: internal_handle
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the internal_handle column of the [AS_CORE].navigation_item table. This is tracked whenever a user accesses a page in the the Academic Suite (eg. When either a PAGE_ACCESS or COURSE_ACCESS event occurs). This will be NULL for events other than PAGE_ACCESS and COURSE_ACCESS. Internal system identifier for the event. This field corresponds to the unique ID in the NAVIGATION_ITEM table. Not all page requests correspond to a navigation item, so this field may often appear blank. If this field is empty, check the CONTENT_PK1 field. If the page accessed displayed content, the primary key for the piece of content will appear in that field.

columns.name: content_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table to indicate the Course Content this activity is associated with. This will be NULL if the activity is not Course Content related. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1. This field is populated when the EVENT_TYPE is CONTENT_ACCESS.

columns.name: data
columns.description: This contains any free-form text data associated with the event. Data related to the event. This field provides additional information on the event. Each event uses this field, if at all, in different ways. In many instances, the data included in this field is a value that is easily deduced. In some instances, the value in the data field is a number, such as _1_1 or _29_1. These are associated with an EVENT_TYPE of TAB_ACCESS. The first number is an ID that references a tab or a module (the second number can be ignored). The ID number that refers to a tab can be found in the user interface by scrolling over the tab. The ID number appears as part of the URL in the status bar.The ID number that refers to a module can be found in the same manner. Scroll over the Maximize, Minimize, or Edit button associated with a module. The ID number will appear as part of the URL in the status bar. Please note that the Detach Module button returns a different ID number and should be ignored.

columns.name: timestamp
columns.description: This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This indicates the status of the event. Value values are success (1) or failure (0). The values come from the TrackingEvent.Status enumeration.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: This is a reference to the primary key of the user session associated with this activity. Identifies the user session that initiated the action. A session is simply a browser connection to the system launched from an end-user machine.

columns.name: ip_address
columns.description: IP address from which the event was generated (optional).

tables.description: An AttributeDefinition contains the meta-data describing an attribute of an entity within the system. These attributes can be user-defined or system attributes. The template and form framework uses these definitions to map fields to their attributes, and the persistence system uses these definitions to determine where to load and store an entity's attribute values.

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.name: name
columns.description: This is the name of the attribute definition, must be unique within the entity type's namespace.

columns.name: label
columns.description: This is the default label for the attribute definition. DEFAULT=label.

columns.name: description
columns.description: This is the description of the attribute definition.

columns.name: entity_datatype
columns.description: This is the string key for datatype of the entity that owns the attribute.

columns.name: value_type
columns.description: This is the localized datatype. Enumerated String containing typing information for the attribute value. DEFAULT=MSTR.

columns.name: attribute_def_type
columns.description: This is the type of attribute. Cor = Core, Cus= Custom, Sys = System.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This is the current status of the AttributeDefinition. The status indicates whether or not the definition has been deployed for a data object. Dpl = Deployed, Def = Defined, Dep = Deprecated.

columns.name: is_external
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this attribute's value comes from an external system and not from forms. DEFAULT=Y.

columns.name: is_secure
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this attribute is a secured attribute. DEFAULT=N.

columns.name: is_securable
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this attribute is a securable attribute. DEFAULT=Y.

columns.name: is_system_required
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this attribute is required to be present on a form. DEFAULT=N.

columns.name: user_visible_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this attribute should be included in user-facing attribute lists. If false, this attribute is considered internal. DEFAULT=Y.

columns.name: writable_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether the attribute's value can be edited. DEFAULT=Y.

columns.name: column_name_2
columns.description: This is the name of the second column in which the attribute is stored. For multicolumn attributes.

columns.name: column_name_3
columns.description: This is the name of the third column in which the attribute is stored. For multicolumn attributes.

columns.name: date_added
columns.description: This is the date time when the attribute was added.

columns.name: date_modified
columns.description: This is the date time when the attribute was last modified.

columns.name: soft_limit

columns.description: No longer used in Learn 9.1.

columns.description: This is the datetime that the course starts to be available to access.

columns.description: This is the datetime that the course stops to be available to access.

columns.description: This is the datetime when the enrollment to the course can be started.

columns.description: Number of days that Students may access the course after enrollment. Useful for self-paced learning.

columns.name: fee
columns.description: This field is not used

columns.name: enroll_access_code
columns.description: This is the access code/password for students to use when enrolling to the course.

columns.name: banner_url
columns.description: This is the URL where the course banner image is stored at. Link to an image that will display at the top of the course.

columns.name: banner_alt
columns.description: This is the ALT text for the course banner image.

columns.name: institution_name
columns.description: The institution name associated with this course (not used?)

columns.name: reg_level_ind
columns.description: This field is used for the Blackboard.com service. It has not relevance outside of the Blackboard.com site. This field is not used

columns.name: navigation_style
columns.description: This is the navigation menu style that is set for the course. Determines whether the Course Menu uses buttons or text links.

columns.name: textcolor
columns.description: This is the text color used for text in the Course Menu.

columns.name: background_color
columns.description: This is the background color that is set for the Course Menu.

columns.name: collapsible_ind
columns.description: Determines whether or not the Course Menu can be consolidated to show just the top headings or expanded to show subheads. This field is not used. Original intention: This flag determines whether or not users of a course should be allowed to 'collapse' (slide into the side) the navigation links which appear on the left hand side of the course page.

columns.name: allow_guest_ind
columns.description: This is the flag that indicates if guest access is allowed.

columns.name: catalog_ind
columns.description: This field is not used

columns.name: lockout_ind
columns.description: This field is not used. Original intent: lockout all but administrator user from the course. Indicates if access to the course or organization has been restricted. If set to Y access to the course or organization will be restricted based on the END_DATE and START_DATE.

columns.name: desc_page_ind
columns.description: This field is not used

columns.name: available_ind
columns.description: This is the flag that indicates if this course is set to be available. If honor_term_avail_ind is true, this flag is ignored and this course's availability is determined by its associated term available_ind.

columns.name: allow_observer_ind
columns.description: This is the flag that indicates if observers are allowed for this course.

columns.name: show_banner_ind
columns.description: Determines whether or not the course banner should be shown or hidden in an Ultra Course. A null value here means that a choice has not yet been made to show or hide the course banner and will be effectively treated as hidden ("N") by the java code.

columns.name: default_content_view
columns.description: This is the view option that decides how the course content view looks like. T = Text Only I = Icon Only X = Icon and Text

columns.name: locale
columns.description: The locale (language) in which the course should be delivered - see is_locale_enforced. A null value means 'use system default'

columns.name: is_locale_enforced
columns.description: Values:Y/N: If Y then the locale will be forced to locale regardless of what the user's personal preferences have set for their locale

columns.name: asmt_upgrade_version
columns.description: The assessment data has to go through a number of runtime upgrade steps before assessments are usable in a course. This field records the current upgrade-state of the assessments data within this course.

columns.name: asmt_upgrade_flags
columns.description: After any import or restore operation the asmt_upgrade_version is set back to 0 and any new data re-upgraded. There are certain parts of the upgrade which do not have to run in this case (i.e. the upgrade is only required once per course, not after each import operation). This field is used to store those flags to avoid re-running pieces of the upgrade

columns.name: honor_term_avail_ind
columns.description: if Y then use the term for available_ind; if N then use those fields from this table. (Note that duration implicitly affects availability through fields such as startdate and enddate but those are only controlled by the term when course.duration=T)

columns.name: course_theme_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].course_theme table. It is the course theme that is used for the course.

columns.name: import_task_pk1
columns.description: The latest queued task pk1 which is import/restore/copy into this course. it is overwritten if multiple ones are queued. This field is transient so not be included in course copy or content exchange operations

columns.name: uuid
columns.description: A unique (generated) identifier for this course. Sent as the context_id in LTI launch requests.

columns.name: copy_from_uuids
columns.description: The source course uuid(s) on copy. This could be a comma-separated list. Sent as the context_id_history in LTI launch requests. Configured to hold up to 10.

columns.name: course_view_option
columns.description: This is course view option flag. It's different from ultra_status flag, this flag control if instructor can change the course view or change directly by admin, while ultra_status just indicate the current course view of this course is. Also, if the course ultra_status is in ULTRA_DECIDED state, then this flag will be ignored. If null, then the default value depends on the system-wide ultra setting: If ultra is ON then null is effectively 'I' If ultra is OFF then null is effectively 'C'

columns.name: ultra_status
columns.description: This is the flag indicating if the course is classic, ultra, or ultra preview. Note that updates to this field are controlled in java code so please do not blindly change it directly. Specifically you can only perform these transitions: N->C, N->U, N->P, C->U, C->P, P->U, P->C, U->NOTHING. You cannot go back once you pick U The NULL value, which represents classic, will be left for all the legacy courses and treated the same as classic

columns.name: is_closed_ind
columns.description: This is the flag indicating if the course is closed for student access. Even if the course is closed, the course is still listed in the student's course listing. The NULL value will be interpreted as N

columns.name: convert_task_pk1
columns.description: The latest queued task pk1 which is a course conversion. it is overwritten if multiple ones are queued. This field is transient so not be included in course copy or content exchange operations

columns.name: ultra_conversion_report_id
columns.description: The identifier for the conversion report when the course was converted from original to Ultra. This field is transient so not be included in content exchange operations

columns.name: owner
columns.description: Indicates which system is the source of truth for the record. Defaults to Learn if unset.

columns.name: foundations_id
columns.description: The ID of this course in Foundations

columns.name: progress_tracking_ind
columns.description: Indicates if the course is set to track student progress. Null values will be treated as 'N'

columns.name: catalog_video_url
columns.description: This is the URL for preview of course to show within catalog listing.

columns.description: The version number of this object. For Learn-owned rows, this is incremented any time the record is written. Defaults to 0 if unset.

tables.description: Contains object lifecycle events (eg. user lifecycle), which tracks object creation, modification, and deletion.

columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.description: This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred.

columns.description: The datatype of the object that this event concerns.

columns.description: The id of the object that this event concerns. For example, a users pk id. Note that we do not have any FK references to any object tables, because there could be various types of objects being tracked and also we do not want any sort of cascadible behavior.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: The type of event this represents. C: Created - Object created U: Updated - Object modified D: Deleted - Object removed

columns.name: status
columns.description: The status of the event record. Used when processing the event queue. U: Unprocessed - Unprocessed event I: In-process - Event is being processed

columns.name: extended_data
columns.description: This contains any data associated with the event to provide additional information. If provided, the data is interpreted differently based on the source and type of the event. This data is stored as delimited key/value pairs.

tables.description: A child table to the event table. This tracks the details of an object modification such as the object property that was updated, and its old and new values. For example, if a user record's address property was modified and tracked via a corresponding modification event record, an entry in this table would contain the address as the property and the old and new addresses as the old and new values.

columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.description: This is a foreign key to the event.pk1.

columns.description: The name of the object property. In the case of a user object, this corresponds to the property names defined in UserDef and UserInfoDef

columns.name: old_value
columns.description: The previous, pre-update value of this property

columns.name: new_value
columns.description: The new value of this property

columns.description: Defines the entitlement required to access the item. Entitlement required to use this navitem. There are many entitlements in the entitlement table to chose from, e.g., system.admin.VIEW, Modify, etc

columns.description: Top level for groupings of navigation items. Used to group navigation items together

columns.description: Address of the application in the file system. URL to access the target item.

columns.description: This the bit mask that determines if the tool is enabled or not. NAVITEM_COURSE = 0x00000001, NAVITEM_ORG = 0x00000002, BBSUPPORT_ONLY = 0x000000040, NONE = 0x00000000, DISABLED = 0x00000020 ALL = 0xffffffff.

columns.description: Image or icon connected to the navigation item.

columns.description: User-visible description - may be a key to a language string.

columns.description: Groups navigation items under the Family heading.

columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.description: This is customized label. If set it will override the label.

columns.name: visible_ind
columns.description: Determines whether or not the item is visible to users. if 'N', this is equivalent to disabling the nav item, but not in all situations.

tables.description: This table contains definition and detailed information of a rubric. Rubrics are owned by Learn Courses or Outcomes Work Contexts.

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.name: work_ctx_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary of the [AS_CORE].work_ctx table. It represents the Work Context that owns this Rubric.

columns.name: course_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].course_main table. It is the course that the rubric was created from.

columns.name: parent_pk1
columns.description: This is a self-referencing foreign key for this table. It is set only for Rubrics owned by the Outcomes Evidence Repository and references the Learn Rubric from which this was copied.

columns.name: title
columns.description: This is the title of the rubric.

columns.name: rubric_desc
columns.description: This is the description of the rubric.

columns.name: contact
columns.description: This is text entered by the user indicating contact information for the person reponsible for this Rubric. This is useful in Outcomes where Rubrics can be made Public and shared with the entire institution.

columns.name: version
columns.description: This is the version of the rubric. It starts at 1 when the rubric is created and increment by 1 everytime the rubric is modified.

columns.name: creator_user_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].users table. It is the user who created the rubric.

columns.name: type
columns.description: This is the type of the rubric. N=Numeric, T=non-numeric(text), R=Numeric Range, P=Percentage, Q=Percentage Range.

columns.name: status
columns.description: This is the status of the rubric. D=Draft, A=Active, I=Inactive.

columns.name: public_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates whether the rubric is public. An Outcomes Rubric must be marked public if it is to be available for use outside the Outcomes context in which it is defined. Learn Rubrics do not use this field.

columns.name: deleted_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates whether the rubric is available for use. Rubrics can be 'soft-deleted' in which case this flag is set to 'Y' or 'hard-deleted' in which case the row is deleted from this table. A 'soft-deleted' rubric can no longer be directly used in the application but the row will continue to exist in the database so that existing evaluations can still internally use the definition to render themselves properly.

columns.name: max_value
columns.description: This is the maximum points that this rubric awards.

columns.name: keywords
columns.description: This is free-form text entered by the user and used as a tag for search and classification.

columns.name: dtcreated
columns.description: This is the datetime when the rubric was created.

columns.name: dtmodified
columns.description: This is the datetime when the rubric was last modified.

columns.name: ai_state
columns.description: Indicates whether the rubric is AI-generated

columns.name: ai_accepting_user_pk1
columns.description: The user who accepted the AI-generated rubric

columns.name: extended_data
columns.description: Used to store arbitrary properties for this item

columns.name: lor_rubric_pk1
columns.description: The object hosting the root Learning Object Repository item

columns.name: lor_sync_date
columns.description: Time associated Learning Object Repository synchronization was last completed.

columns.name: soft_time_limit
columns.description: Unit in minutes. In the case of tests with a (time_limit), if this is null then it means there is no soft-time-limit and behaves same as Learn 9.1. If it's not null, user will receive an alert if the (soft_time_limit) expires. Depending on the value of (timer_completion), user will be forced to submit attempt ((timer_completion) is (H)) or be alerted again but can continue working without deadline ((timer_completion) is (C)) if the (time_limit) expires then. So (soft_time_limit) should be always less than (time_limit) if it's not null, this will be ensured and checked at REST API level.

tables.description: Each question-block is a single row in qti_asi_data where the qti xml contains a list of all the questions it references. This qti_block_mapping reflects that relationship of 1 question block and n questions This table is actually dual-purpose, also supporting random blocks. Each random-block is a single row in qti_asi_data. Historically a random block had a single source pool stored both in the qti xml and in objectbank_pk1. With the support of multiple source pools for a random block, this table augments that column which is being left in the db to avoid any upgrade-time overhead. When used for random blocks we reflect the following relationship. 1 random block and n pools. It is 'ok' to re-use this table because it is modeling a 1 qti_asi_data_pk1 and n qti_asi_data_pk1 style of relationship in both cases.

tables.description: This table contains general information for discussion boards. A conference is a discussion board that acts as a container for various discussion forums. columns.description: This is the foreign key referencing course_main table. If it is null than indicates SYSTEM / institution/community discussions. If it is not null and groups_pk1 is null it is the COURSE discussion. If it is not null and groups_pk1 is not null it is GROUPS discussion.

columns.name: description

tables.description: Stores discussion related stream events to populate the My Blackboard stream viewer

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.name: actor_pk1
columns.description: FK to users.pk1 for the person doing the action - i.e. a comment on a post would set the commenter in actor_pk1. This column will be set to NULL if the user was deleted in which case this row should be ignored.

columns.name: actee_pk1
columns.description: FK to users.pk1 for the person the action was done against - i.e. a comment on a post would set the post-author in actee_pk1. This will be NULL if the stream event is not in response to a particular user or if the user was deleted.

columns.name: crsmain_pk1
columns.description: FK to course_main for the course in which the event occurs. This will be NULL if the stream event occurs within a community discussion board or if the course was deleted.

columns.name: group_pk1
columns.description: FK to groups for the group in which the event occurs. This will be NULL for non group discussion boards or if the group was deleted.

columns.name: event_date
columns.description: Date and time the event occurred.

columns.name: event_modified_date
columns.description: Date and time the event was modified (only set in response to a cascade setnull trigger - see FKs below).

columns.name: course_contents_pk1
columns.description: FK to course_contents.pk1 if the event pertains to a course contents item. This will be NULL if the event does not have a course_contents.pk1 or if the course content was deleted.

columns.name: ultra_group_forum_contents_pk1
columns.description: FK to course_contents.pk1 if the event is fired in a group discussion (real forum). This will be NULL if the forum related to this event is not group disscussion. This column is only used for group discussions in an Ultra course.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: The event type identifier constrained to the below values.

columns.name: event_text
columns.description: Text specific to this event - not the stream text directly, but the dynamic text to substitute into an event-appropriate message when rendering the stream.

columns.name: thread_subject
columns.description: This is the thread subject as of the time when the message was first posted. AB#506329: A task was created to update this value if it ever changes.

columns.name: forum_main_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the forum_main table. This column will be set to NULL if the forum was deleted in which case this row will be ignored for new events and otherwise used to purge existing events from the UI

columns.name: msg_main_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table. This column will be set to null if the msg was deleted in which case the row will be ignored for new events and otherwise used to purge existing events from the UI

columns.name: parent_msg_main_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table for the parent thread message.

columns.name: non_group_thread_msg_main_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table for the top thread message that is not associated to a group. This applies only to ULTRA and is used to manage discussion subscription.

columns.name: top_level_response_users_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table for the actor of the top level response of the message.

columns.name: actor_acts_as_instructor_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the actor of the message acts as an instructor.

columns.name: highlight_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the user name should be highlighted in the stream as moderator or manager. An extra check is done in the java code to check if it still should be highlighted.

columns.name: indirect_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the discussion is within the INDIRECT content area (In Ultra courses an INDIRECT courseToc is created which is not 'visible' to the users in the UI. Things like conversations-on-content are created within this folder as a forum link but need to be presented differently in the stream - as a conversation and not a discussion)

columns.name: delta_due_date
columns.description: Indicates whether the user or group has a due date exception. A value equal to zero means the item will never be marked as late, and a value not equal to zero means the new due date is the gradable item's due date plus this value, which specifies a duration in minutes (can be positive or negative). If this value and fixed_due_date are both null, then there is no due date exception. Both cannot be simultaneously non-null.

columns.description: Indicates whether the user or group has a due date exception. A non-null value represents the new due date for this user/group's gradable item. If this value and delta_due_date are both null, then there is no due date exception. Both cannot be simultaneously non-null.

tables.description: This table contains individual notification item information.

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.description: This is the identifier of the parent item. If this notification is conceptually subordinate to another notifications - as Assignment Submitted is subordinate to Assignment Due, for example - then this column contains the id of the parent notification.

columns.name: dtcreated
columns.description: This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred. The date on which the item was first added.

columns.description: This is the title of the notification item. This will be visible to the user in the UI.

columns.name: crsmain_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_main table.

columns.name: owner_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table. A foreign key reference to the user who created this item, or is responsible for it.

columns.name: source_id
columns.description: This is the source or content item that originated this notification item. An identifier that uniquely specifies the item on which we're notifying. It's the responsibility of the individual subsystems to ensure that this uniqueness.

columns.name: crs_contents_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table. This represents the content item from the course or organization that originated this notification. This will be populated when the notification is generated by content, otherwise null.

columns.name: parent_content_pk1
columns.description: This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table. This represents the parent of the content item that originated this notification.

columns.name: source_type
columns.description: This is the source type of the notification item. The class of event this represents: an assignment event, or an assessment event, or a content event, etc

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: This is the type of event for this notification item, ie. AVAILABLE or OVERDUE. The specifi A=c type of event, within the course_type, that this represent: Assignment Available, or example, or Assignment Submitted S=Scheduled; A= Available.

columns.name: type
columns.description: This is the type of notification item. Whether this is a Scheduled or an Available notification. S=Scheduled; A=Available.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: The time when the action happened. The date on which the notification period should begin - which usually maps to the date on which the item will become available. If this is specified, we won't display notification until this date is reached. Note that this is not related to adaptive release rules - those will be evaluated separately and independently.

columns.name: due_date
columns.description: This is the due date associated with the source that originated this notification. The date on which this notification is due. Internally, the due date is used to figure out when to send reminders, and also to determine whether transform DUE events into OVERDUE events.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: The time when the action ended. The date on which the notification period should end - which usually maps to the date on which the item will become unavailable. If this is specified, we won't display notification after this date is reached. Note that this is not related to adaptive release rules - those will be evaluated separately and independently.

columns.name: data_pending_ind
columns.description: Whether this notification is in the midst of being created - ie, whether it is waiting for its associated recipients to be created. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification is in the midst of being created - ie, whether it is waiting for its associated recipients to be created.

columns.name: can_replace_ind
columns.description: Whether this notification can be replaced by incoming notifications that would normally obviate them. See Notification Replacement for more details. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification can be replaced by incoming notifications that would normally obviate them.

columns.name: important_ind
columns.description: This is, unfortunately, a very nebulous name for a very specific concept. An important marker indicates that, during a blitz (which is to say, a mass notification) this notification should always be sent out to its recipients, no matter what. See Notification Blitz for more details. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item is important.

columns.name: semi_important_ind
columns.description: An semi-important marker indicates that notifications will be treated as important for new enrolled users prior to the start date, so that notification can be sent out to those new enrolled users. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item is semi-important.

columns.name: override_setting_ind
columns.description: Whether this notification should ignore any system/user customizations that would normally suppress its dissemination. This is useful for notifications that absolutely, positively must get out there. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item should be delivered to recipients regardless of their individual notification settings.

columns.name: default_receiver_status
columns.description: This represents the status of the default receiver.

columns.name: default_sender_status
columns.description: This represents the status of the default sender.

columns.name: force_notify_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the notification should be forced to be sent regardless the course status.

tables.description: This table contains general information on a list of tools (addressbook, gradebook etc.) that are available in the system.

columns.name: application
columns.description: This is the handle of the tool, used to reference the tool in other database tables/code.

columns.name: large_icon
columns.description: This is the image file name for the icon that displays on the UI for the tool. 50 x 50 pixels.

columns.name: plugins_pk1
columns.description: This is a Foreign Key referencing the primary key of the Building Block that created the tool (if any).

columns.name: blti_placement_pk1
columns.description: This is a Foreign Key referencing the primary key of the Basic LTI placement that created the tool (if any).

columns.name: enabled_mask
columns.description: This the bit mask that determines if the tool is enabled or not. SYSTEM = 0x00000001, COURSE = 0x00000002, ORG = 0x00000004, COURSE_GROUP = 0x00000008, ORG_GROUP = 0x00000010, NAVITEM_COURSE = 0x00000001, NAVITEM_ORG = 0x00000002, NONE = 0x00000000, ALL = 0xffffffff.

columns.name: prev_enabled_mask
columns.description: The previous configured value of enabled_mask. This is used when enabling/disabling Building Blocks so that when a Building Block is disabled, then enabled, the previous customizations are retained.

columns.name: ssl_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicates if the tool needs to run under SSL.

columns.name: relabel_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if this tool has been relabeled.

columns.name: label
columns.description: This is the localized label of the tool (almost always a bundle key reference).

columns.name: pk1
columns.description: This is the surrogate primary key for the table.

columns.name: small_icon
columns.description: This is the path and image file name for the small icon for the tool. 12 x 12 pixels.

columns.name: tree_icon
columns.description: This is the path and image file name for the tree icon for the tool. 16 x 16 pixels.

columns.name: description
columns.description: This the localized description of the tool (almost always a bundle key reference).

columns.name: allow_guest_mask
columns.description: This is the bit mask that indicates if guest is allowed to use this tool. SYSTEM = 0x00000001, COURSE = 0x00000002, ORG = 0x00000004, COURSE_GROUP = 0x00000008, ORG_GROUP = 0x00000010, NAVITEM_COURSE = 0x00000001, NAVITEM_ORG = 0x00000002, NONE = 0x00000000, ALL = 0xffffffff.

columns.name: allow_observer_mask
columns.description: This is the bit mask that indicates if observers are allowed to use this tool. SYSTEM = 0x00000001, COURSE = 0x00000002, ORG = 0x00000004, COURSE_GROUP = 0x00000008, ORG_GROUP = 0x00000010, NAVITEM_COURSE = 0x00000001, NAVITEM_ORG = 0x00000002, NONE = 0x00000000, ALL = 0xffffffff.

columns.name: name
columns.description: This is the localized name of the tool (almost always a bundle key reference). It should contain the same initial value as the label column.

columns.name: can_relabel_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool can be relabeled.

columns.name: can_allow_guest_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if guests are allowed to use the tool. This column is used in conjunction with allow_guest_mask.

columns.name: can_allow_observer_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if guests are allowed to use the tool. This column is used in conjunction with allow_observer_mask.

columns.name: can_configure_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool can be configured.

columns.name: configure_url
columns.description: This contains the configuration URL for the tool.

columns.name: system_tool_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool is a system tool.

columns.name: course_tool_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool is a course level tool.

columns.name: org_tool_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool is a organization tool.

columns.name: group_tool_ind
columns.description: This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the tool is a tool for group.

tables.description: This table contains FKs to entities that can have VTBE/BbML associated with them. At most one FK may be non-null. When bulk delete ocurrs, such as when a course is deleted or when an attempt is deleted, the FK is set to null, and will be cleaned up in a different thread. So the state where all FKs, crsmain_pk1 excluded, are null is very short-lived and is required so that cleanup work which can caused delays is done asynchronously. As new entities are added which can have VTBE/BbML associated to them, a new FK column is added to this table. Note: This table allows tools with 1 or more VTBE fields to register as a content owner so that they can be associated generically to other objects in the database. As such, the table is not video integration specific and can be moved to core in the future.
